question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{x^2} = |x|
$$

Also, we notice that $4, x^2,$ and $y^2$ are all perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{4{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}}} & =\sqrt{\frac{{2}^{2}{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot x\cdot x}{y\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2\cdot x\cdot 2\cdot x}{y\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2x}{y}\cdot \frac{2x}{y}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{2x}{y})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(\frac{2x}{y})}^{2}} & =|\frac{2x}{y}| \\  & =\frac{|2x|}{|y|} \\  & =\frac{|2|\cdot |x|}{|y|} \\  & =\frac{2|x|}{|y|}\end{aligned}
$$
